notes:
Four walkthrough bullets, all four of them real, and a six-bullet 'Notes' section after the walkthrough that contains no steps at all -- solo only, a 15 minute arena timer, which avatar may be used, buffing outside the fight, pet food, and a warning that a re-obtained fork no longer earns the teleport. Those bullets restart at [1]; none of them is recorded as a step and none of their numbers appears in source_bullets.

The one thing this page never says is which zone the protocrystal is in. The Description calls it 'the protocrystal in Ifrit's Cauldron' and Note 6 calls the destination 'the Cloister', but the Cloister's own name appears nowhere on the page. Steps 3 and 4 are therefore written with NO zone rather than with a wrong one: a nil-zone row matches everywhere, and 'Fire Protocrystal' is distinctive enough to land where it belongs. Writing 'Ifrit's Cauldron' would have resolved cleanly and then drawn nothing, which is the worse failure.

Bullet 2 is a genuine interaction and not padding -- trading the fork back to Dodmos is the page's own transport to the arena -- but it is optional: you can walk in instead, and Note 6 says the NPC stops teleporting you once you re-obtain a fork. It sits on Dodmos directly after step 1, so it shares that marker either way. The Mini Tuning Fork of Fire is item 1544, not a key item (it does not resolve as one); bullet 1 grants it and it is not in the Reward list, so it is honest evidence for step 1. 'Summoner Level 20 or higher' is both gates.

ADVERSARY (stage D): demoted high -> medium. The reading above asserts "The one thing this page never says is which zone the protocrystal is in", and that is not true -- the Description says outright "Ringing it upon the protocrystal in Ifrit's Cauldron", which names the zone step 3 stands in. The rest of the argument (that the arena the fight happens in is only ever called "the Cloister") holds, so step 4's null zone is right. I may only remove, null or downgrade, so step 3's zone is left null rather than filled in, and the quest is demoted instead: a rung whose zone the page supplies and the ladder omits is a gap a human should close, not a clean read. Everything else survived the five attacks -- evidence is granted at bullet 1 and is not in the Reward list, the fork is items and not evidence on the two trades so no item is evidence twice, bullet 2 is correctly optional, the order is the page's order, and all four targets are bare names taken from the page.

steps.note: a lift to the arena, not a requirement -- you may walk in instead, and the Notes say a re-obtained fork no longer buys the teleport. The fork survives this trade; bullet 3 still spends it.

no zone is recorded on purpose: the page names only 'Ifrit's Cauldron' (in the Description) and 'the Cloister' (in Note 6), never the zone the protocrystal actually stands in, so a nil zone that matches everywhere beats a named one that would match nothing
one-on-one, no party; 15 minute limit, and the Notes say only Carbuncle (or, apparently unintentionally, Siren) may be summoned. Same unnamed arena zone as step 3.

notes:
Eight bullets and no key items anywhere in the walkthrough, so this ladder has no evidence at all -- every rung is a place you go, and the runtime falls back on the session latch throughout. That is the honest answer here rather than a reach.

Deliberately NO obtain step for the Hydrangea. It is a header Item Req you are expected to bring, bought at the auction house or farmed from Mount Zhayolm hilltrolls, so making 'you hold a Hydrangea' evidence would shove the high-water mark past the two Mount Zhayolm cutscenes for anybody who shopped first -- exactly the wrong-marker failure the evidence rules exist to stop. It stays an items requirement on steps 4 and 5, with the three drop sources recorded as mobs on step 4 even though they live in Mount Zhayolm and that step is in Whitegate.

Bullets 4 and 5 both spend a Hydrangea and the page never says whether Fari-Wari hands it back, so whether one flower or two are needed is genuinely unreadable -- hence medium. The items lists are right either way, because they state what you must be holding to perform each step.

Bullets 7 and 8 come after the completing cutscene in bullet 6 and only collect things already in the Reward list (the Gadalar Trust, the Mercenary Camp Entry Slip), so they are optional epilogue on the same NPC and the same marker. Both Mount Zhayolm clicks are 18:00-06:00 only, and bullet 8 waits for a day change; none of that is visible to the addon. 'Gadalar must be present in Al Zahbi' is a Besieged NPC-presence condition with no slot in the schema and no observable predicate. The Mercenary Camp Entry Slip does not resolve as a key item, which costs nothing here because it is a reward and never used.

steps.note: in the Shararat Teahouse; Gadalar must be standing in Al Zahbi for this to be offered

18:00-06:00 game time only, which the addon cannot see. Start it before 05:00 or there is not time to read the dialogue and trigger step 3 in the same night. Voidwatch teleport lands on it; Escape from Halvung lands just north.
southeast portion near the coastal cliffs; 18:00-06:00 only. The cutscene drops you back in Aht Urhgan Whitegate.
the three hilltrolls drop the Hydrangea in Mount Zhayolm, not here; it is also on the auction house. The page does not say whether he returns the flower, so a second may be needed for step 5.
the same Withered Petals as step 3, but this one does not have to be at night. Medium only because of the one-or-two-Hydrangeas ambiguity between bullets 4 and 5.
the Imperial Gold Piece arrives here, but it is in the Reward list, so it proves the quest over rather than this step done
after the quest is already finished; unlocks Trust: Gadalar, which is a listed reward
one game day later, for the Mercenary Camp Entry Slip -- also a listed reward, and the day change is unobservable

notes:
Three bullets, and the middle one is three steps. The page says outright that the three ??? 'can be found in any order', so they share a group and all three draw at once; a strict ladder would mark whichever I happened to list first and leave the other two dark until the player stumbled onto them. Two are in Marjami Ravine and the third is across the zone line in Dho Gates, so each carries its own zone -- one step, one zone -- and each keeps the grid the page gives it.

None of the three can carry a marker, because ??? never can, but they keep their rungs: the ladder still knows there are three places to go and where they are. Every indented sub-bullet under them is route directions (which vine to climb, which tunnel, which wall to follow) and belongs in notes, not in steps.

Nothing after step 1 is observable. The page calls what you collect only 'water samples' and never names an item or key item for them, so no evidence is recorded on any group member and none is invented; the whole quest hangs on the Ravine water testing kit granted at step 1. Quest Reqs '"Climbing"' is the Adoulin traverse ability, not a job and not a level -- there is no gate for it and it gates two of the three ???. Fame 'Seekers of Adoulin' is not one of the nine fame regions, so the region is null and only the raw string is kept.

steps.note: at Frontier Bivouac #1; the page gives no grid reference for him

next to the ergon locus, and it needs 'Climbing'. North from Bivouac #1, up the hill past the colonization reive, straight to the tunnel, climb the vine, then northeast and down the vine to the waterfall.
east side of the river. From Bivouac #2 head southeast and take the tunnel from (J-10); turn right the moment you leave the tunnel -- a bush hides the area.
west side of the stream, and it needs 'Climbing'. In from the Frontier Station in Marjami Ravine, right at the fork, up the vine, then along the left wall past a small pond to the river.

notes:
Nine bullets, of which bullets 3, 4 and 7 are outcomes rather than actions -- the zone-in cutscene fires by itself, Cannau spawns by herself, and she stops at (F-8) by herself -- and most of bullet 5's sub-bullets are escort tactics (stop her by talking, kill what she pulls, cure her before she blood-aggros). They fold into notes.

The wiki's 'Eldieme Necropolis' does not resolve; the zone is 'The Eldieme Necropolis' and that is what is written on all three steps inside it.

The door at (H-8) gets its own rung even though it can never carry a marker, because that rung is where the Magicked astrolabe requirement actually bites, and the ladder is worth more knowing about it than not. The page's alternative -- 'bring someone with you' to flip the switch -- is a person and not an item, so it cannot go in items_alt: items_partial is set and the OR branch is flagged rather than faked. The page never names the door, only 'the door at (H-8)', so the target is none rather than an invented 'Door: ...' string.

Cannau is a spawned escort NPC and she does resolve, so the (F-8) conversation is markable and carries the Completion certificate -- the quest's only observable, and it is granted exactly there. The 30 minute timer and the fact that she despawns and voids the escort if you are slow are notes; neither is expressible.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 3: the second option is a player, not an item, which is why items_partial is set.

steps.note: in from Batallia Downs (I-10). The cutscene fires on zoning in and Cannau spawns after it; the 30 minute clock starts here.

The page calls it only 'the door at (H-8)' and never names it, so no target is claimed. Either hold a Magicked astrolabe or bring a second person to flip the switch Cannau runs west to this door; talk to her to halt her and clear what she has pulled.
past the gate she takes either the north or the south path to (F-8) and stops on her own. Speak to her quickly -- if she despawns first you get no credit.
10,000 gil the first time only; repeatable thereafter

notes:
Bullets 1, 2 and 3 are one step, not three. The compatibility test, the follow-up conversation and the handover of the Magic trash all happen at Chululu, and consecutive rungs on one NPC are one marker anyway. Bullet 1 is where the real cost is -- three separate game days of asking her to test you against a nearby player, typing that player's name as the password, then a fourth day before she offers the quest -- and none of it is observable, so the whole approach collapses into a single rung whose evidence is the Magic trash key item she finally hands over. Her own warning is kept: if she talks about 'spreading the wonder of tarut cards' that is All in the Cards, so answer no and speak to her again.

Bullets 4, 5 and 6 are exposition and routing for bullet 7 -- where the Incinerator is, that a Garlaige Key opens it, and which two Banishing Gates to pass -- so all four merge into the Crematory Hatch trade. The key is NOT evidence: the hatch consumes it, so holding it proves nothing is finished, only that you are ready. It is an items requirement with the Fallen Evacuee recorded as its drop source.

Mashira is a separate rung from the hatch because he is a separate entity in a separate room, and the Magic trash dies with him, so nothing is observable there. Bullet 10 sits under a '== Notes ==' heading and only recommends stacking Making Amens! to avoid farming the key twice; it is not a step. The [TABLE] the prepass flagged is a row of map thumbnails and holds nothing.

steps.note: have her test your compatibility with a nearby player on three DIFFERENT game days -- type that player's name as the password -- then speak to her one game day later to be given the quest and the Magic trash. If she offers to spread the wonder of tarut cards, that is All in the Cards; say no and talk again.
map 3, past the first two Banishing Gates. The key drops from Fallen Evacuee in the rooms right by the zone entrance on map 1. The trade opens the Incinerator Room.
inside the Incinerator Room; the page gives him no grid of his own. He destroys the Magic trash, so nothing is left to observe.

notes:
Six bullets and an unnumbered preamble; three real steps, and a genuinely good little two-anchor ladder for a repeatable errand.

The preamble is a cooldown, not a step: only one Refuel and Replenish or A Mightier Martello per Vana'dielian day across ALL Abyssea areas, and nothing in the packets reports the Vana'diel day. Bullet 2 is the outcome of bullet 1 and supplies its evidence, the Vat of martello fuel. Bullet 3 is 'find a Martello', which is the target of bullet 4's click rather than a step of its own, so the two merge. Bullet 5 is advice about the menu direction disagreeing with the log direction, but its sub-bullet is the load-bearing line -- the full vat silently becomes an Empty fuel vat -- and that is step 2's evidence and the reason this quest can be tracked at all.

'Martello' resolves as an entity, so the middle step is markable and will draw on every martello in the zone. That is correct rather than sloppy: bullet 3 says any of them will do, and they cluster around the Confluxes. The Machine Outfitter's zone suffix folds away to a key shared by every Abyssea area's outfitter, so the step's own zone is the only thing keeping steps 1 and 3 pointed at the right one. Fame 'atah' is an Abyssea area code, not one of the nine fame regions, so the region is null and only the raw string is kept. The zoning warning -- zone once and the key item is gone and you start over -- is a note.

steps.note: near the zone entrance; choose 'Assist with replenishment'. Do not zone after this -- zoning destroys the key item and you start again. Only one of these quests per Vana'dielian day, across all of Abyssea.

any martello in the zone, usually near a Conflux; it works even at 100% health. Choose 'Prepare to replenish martello', confirm, and stand in the direction the MENU gives, not the one the log gives. The vat quietly becomes an Empty fuel vat, which the page only mentions in a sub-bullet.
the cruor paid depends on which martello you chose
